## Motivation

This PR is powered by [KDA](https://github.com/NVlabs/kda) team. MegaMoE is the largest prefill cost in the BF16 TP8/EP8 deployment: about 68 ms of a 131 ms 8K-token TTFT on rank 0. For BF16 prefill shards DeepGEMM's heuristic picks BLOCK_M 192 (`2,192,48,128,2`), sized for uniformly spread routing. Muse Spark routing is skewed, and on GB300 `2,240,40,128,2` is faster for these shards. DeepGEMM reads `DG_MEGA_MOE_TILES` on every MegaMoE launch; an empty value keeps its heuristic.

## Modifications

- `srt/layers/muse_spark/muse_spark_megamoe.py`: `_tile_override` asks DeepGEMM's `get_block_m_for_mega_moe` for the launch's tile (LRU-cached); only when it returns 192 for `bf16xbf16` does `_megamoe_tiles` set `DG_MEGA_MOE_TILES=2,240,40,128,2` around that one launch and reset it afterwards, including on exceptions
- NVFP4, decode and small prefill shards (smaller heuristic tiles) and a user-set `DG_MEGA_MOE_TILES` are left alone
- `test_muse_spark_megamoe_tiles.py` (new): the override rules and env scoping on any GPU; on SM100 it pins the installed heuristic, checks that DeepGEMM honours the override and that BF16 output is bitwise identical with either tile. Registered on H100 and B200

## Accuracy Tests

- BLOCK_M only changes how rows are split into tiles, not the K-loop order, epilogue or combine; the registered test checks bitwise-identical output with 192 and 240
- GSM8K (sgl-eval, 1319 questions, BF16 TP8/EP8, 8 runs per side): 93.71% vs 93.55% (-0.16 pt, 95% CI [-0.41, +0.08]); Low Latency recipe -0.08 pt (4 runs per side); greedy replay identical to main

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel on GB300, EP4, 256 experts, top-k 8, expert popularity lognormal (sigma = skew), rank-max time, two jobs:

| Tokens per rank | Skew | BLOCK_M 192 | BLOCK_M 240 | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2048 | 1.2 | 1933 us | 1788 us | 1.081x / 1.083x |
| 2048 | 0.7 | 1772 us | 1664 us | 1.065x / 1.066x |
| 2048 | uniform | 1763 us | 1769 us | 0.996x / 0.998x |
| 1024 | 0.7 | 1177 us | 1124 us | 1.048x / 1.048x |

BF16 model vs main (2x GB300, TP8/EP8, cookbook GB300 High Throughput recipe, 64 requests per point, two pairs):

| Point | Pair 1 | Pair 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8K C1 TTFT | 1.035x (131.3 -> 126.9 ms) | 1.024x (130.4 -> 127.4 ms) |
| 8K C8 TTFT | 1.043x | 1.021x |
| mixed C1 / C8 TTFT | 1.037x / 1.041x | 1.025x / 1.022x |

- Rank-0 MegaMoE time per 8K request: 68.1 -> 63.7 ms and 67.3 -> 64.5 ms
- Decode ITL within 0.3% of main; no serving point regresses
- Low Latency recipe (DFlash, one pair): 8K C1 TTFT 1.034x [1.032, 1.037] (145.6 -> 140.8 ms), verify-step time 1.002x-1.032x, accept lengths unchanged
- NVFP4 is unchanged (the override only applies to `bf16xbf16`)
- Measured on GB300 only. The override also applies to B200 and B300 BF16 (same EP8 shards); B200 speed is untested, and the gain depends on skewed routing (uniform routing is 0.2-0.4% slower in the kernel table above)
- Happy to limit it to SM103 (B300/GB300) if reviewers prefer, or keep it on B200 if someone can measure there

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -8,14 +8,24 @@
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import contextlib
+import functools
 import logging
+import os
 
 import torch
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
 _MEGAMOE_SYMM_BUFFERS: dict = {}
 
+# DeepGEMM reads this on every MegaMoE launch; an empty value keeps its heuristic.
+_TILES_ENV = "DG_MEGA_MOE_TILES"
+# (CTA pair, BLOCK_M, STORE_BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K bytes, epilogue warpgroups). With
+# Muse routing on GB300, BLOCK_M 240 beats the heuristic's 192 for BF16
+# prefill-sized shards; smaller heuristic tiles are kept.
+_BF16_PREFILL_TILES = "2,240,40,128,2"
+
 
 def _dimensions(layer):
     if hasattr(layer, "global_num_experts"):
@@ -306,6 +316,49 @@ def _get_symm_buffer(layer, group, capacity, device):
     return buf
 
 
+@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
+def _heuristic_block_m(num_ranks, num_experts, capacity, num_tokens, top_k, mma_type):
+    import deep_gemm
+
+    return deep_gemm.get_block_m_for_mega_moe(
+        num_ranks=num_ranks,
+        num_experts=num_experts,
+        num_max_tokens_per_rank=capacity,
+        num_tokens=num_tokens,
+        num_topk=top_k,
+        mma_type=mma_type,
+    )
+
+
+def _tile_override(buf, num_tokens):
+    """BF16 prefill tiles for this launch, or None to keep DeepGEMM's choice."""
+    if buf.mma_type != "bf16xbf16" or os.environ.get(_TILES_ENV):
+        # A user-provided DG_MEGA_MOE_TILES always wins.
+        return None
+    block_m = _heuristic_block_m(
+        buf.group.size(),
+        buf.num_experts,
+        buf.num_max_tokens_per_rank,
+        num_tokens,
+        buf.num_topk,
+        buf.mma_type,
+    )
+    return _BF16_PREFILL_TILES if block_m == 192 else None
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def _megamoe_tiles(tiles):
+    if tiles is None:
+        yield
+        return
+    os.environ[_TILES_ENV] = tiles
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        # Keep the key (empty = heuristic) so later launches only replace values.
+        os.environ[_TILES_ENV] = ""
+
+
 @torch.no_grad()
 def forward_megamoe(layer, hidden_states, topk_scores, topk_ids, post_expert_norm):
     """Dispatch sequence shards, run both GEMMs, normalize experts, then combine.
@@ -398,5 +451,7 @@ def forward_megamoe(layer, hidden_states, topk_scores, topk_ids, post_expert_nor
         kernel = deep_gemm.nvfp4_mega_moe
     else:
         kernel = deep_gemm.bf16_mega_moe
-    kernel(y, layer.megamoe_l1_weights, layer.megamoe_l2_weights, buf, **kwargs)
+    # Match the non-null output allocation passed to DeepGEMM.
+    with _megamoe_tiles(_tile_override(buf, y.shape[0])):
+        kernel(y, layer.megamoe_l1_weights, layer.megamoe_l2_weights, buf, **kwargs)
     return y[:n]
